idea: Store one temporary Laurent term, radical, or opaque atom inline; spill to the same ordered growable representation for additional terms.
hypothesis: The profile attributes 51.0697% inclusive sampled cycles to normal forms; Vec cloning and allocation leaf costs motivate reducing temporary vector allocation. This is not a measured speedup prediction.
invariants: Preserve every coefficient, exponent, checked arithmetic operation, insertion order, MAX_TERMS/MAX_RADICAL_TERMS, 64-depth/512-node recognition bounds, and all fallback paths.
No new public scalar representation, persistent cache, predicate stratum, approximation, policy, or serialization change.
The temporary inline containers grow in size; measure allocations, peak RSS, runtime and binary size instead of assuming a net win.
validation: Run the existing full default/all-feature scalar suites, strict scalar/curve Clippy and frozen curve/native matrix before the original unmodified full-board test. Compare public scalar identity witnesses against the 126-case independent Fraction oracle, with separate matched timing/allocation processes. Production isolation, historical capability rows and full reports remain required before retention.
decision: Pending; the broader native-source candidate is not admitted by this experiment.
